findings.title: Unguarded access to mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration can throw when destinationCalendar is empty
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null/undefined/empty. The very next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining: `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")`. Any booking using Google Meet location where the organizer/eventType has no destination calendar configured (a legitimate, common case) will throw a TypeError ("Cannot read properties of undefined") and crash booking creation. Previously this used optional chaining (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`), so this is a regression introduced by the array migration.

findings.title: Broken calendarId fallback logic in updateEvent after destinationCalendar array migration
findings.body: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (null/undefined/empty string, which is a common case when the stored booking reference has no externalCalendarId), the fallback branch searches destinationCalendar entries for one whose `externalId` equals that same falsy value, which will essentially never match a real calendar id. As a result `selectedCalendar` resolves to `undefined` and is passed as `calendarId` to `calendar.events.update(...)`, which will fail or behave unexpectedly. Previously this simply used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` as a sane fallback; the new logic is a functional regression for all update calls lacking an explicit externalCalendarId.

findings.title: Same broken calendarId fallback logic in deleteEvent
findings.body: `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` has the identical defect as in updateEvent: when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, it searches for a destinationCalendar whose externalId equals that same falsy value, which will not match. The code happens to fall back to `defaultCalendarId` ("primary") afterward, but this means any destination calendar other than primary will not be targeted for deletion when no explicit externalCalendarId is passed, silently deleting from the wrong calendar (or failing to delete the actual event).

findings.title: Team members' destination calendars are silently dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);` uses optional chaining. If neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` are set, `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, so the `?.push` call is a no-op and all collected `teamDestinationCalendars` (the whole point of this PR — inviting other hosts' calendars) are discarded. For a COLLECTIVE event where the organizer doesn't have a destination calendar configured but team members do, none of the hosts will get calendar invites, defeating the stated purpose of the PR.

findings.title: Dynamic user lookup lost `organization.slug` selection during loadUsers refactor
findings.body: The refactored `loadUsers` function for the dynamic-booking branch (`!eventTypeId`) selects `{...userSelect.select, credentials: true, metadata: true}` but drops the previously-selected `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` field that existed before this PR. Any downstream code relying on `user.organization.slug` for dynamic/organization-aware bookings will now receive `undefined`, which can cause incorrect behavior or runtime errors later in the booking flow.

findings.title: Silent failure when calendar credential cannot be resolved for a destination calendar
findings.body: In `createAllCalendarEvents`, when a `destination.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found in `this.calendarCredentials` nor in the DB (e.g. deleted/invalid credential), the code falls through without logging an error or recording any failed result — `createdEvent` is simply never pushed. This means a host configured with a destination calendar that has a bad credential silently never gets invited, with no visibility into why, making this hard to diagnose in production.

findings.title: Potential crash passing an unresolved credential to updateEvent
findings.body: In `updateAllCalendarEvents`, when `reference.credentialId` is set but not found locally, the code attempts to fetch it from the DB; if `credentialFromDB` exists but `credentialFromDB.app?.slug` is falsy, `credential` remains `undefined`, yet `result.push(updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId))` is still called unconditionally with the undefined credential. `updateEvent` (via `getCalendar`) expects a valid `CredentialWithAppName` and will likely throw when given `undefined`, crashing the whole reschedule/update Promise.all batch instead of failing gracefully for just that one reference.

findings.title: No test coverage added for the core multi-host destinationCalendar feature
findings.body: Only a pre-existing e2e assertion (`destinationCalendar: null` → `destinationCalendar: []`) was adjusted to match the new array type; no new test was added to verify that a COLLECTIVE event with multiple hosts, each with their own destination calendar, actually results in calendar events being created/updated/deleted on all hosts' calendars. The PR description itself acknowledges 'I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works.' Given this PR changes a widely-used type (`CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar`) across ~20 files, lack of coverage for the primary multi-host scenario is a significant gap.
